THREE THINGS THE BUILD MUST NOT LOSE, all on the ticket:
(1) THE TWO HALVES ARE ONE VOYAGE. Falsifier clause (1): the collapse landing without the verdict-change door is a straight Law 7 breach, because the whole adjudication is that a verdict change gets LOUDER (fired out a door at the moment it happens) rather than quieter (buried at index 1 of a file nothing reads).
(2) RETIRING THE CHAIN KILLS A LIVE PROBE. cairn/devices/tester/probes/the_door_is_the_only_path_in_practice.py triggers on `post_fix >= 20 and unlinked_count > 0`; with nothing writing TRAIL_LINK every post-collapse record reads as unlinked and it fires forever on a finding false by construction. It is a live WATCHME on the ticket that just PROVED, so its retirement is an owner's act with a reason on the record, in the same act — not a deletion.
(3) COMMIT BEFORE COLLAPSE, and it is a build constraint rather than hygiene. The archive claim is 'git keeps every prior version' — measured true (90 of 90 trails git-tracked) but conditional on the commit having happened. A collapse on an uncommitted trail loses the prior record irretrievably. Falsifier clause (2) is that made falsifiable.

SCOPED OUT ON A MEASUREMENT: the artifact/quorum seal path (validations_path_for_artifact) — 0 specimens in 90 trails, so the rule is not written against zero. Reopener is an event: the first quorum-sealed artifact trail.
